greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. May the grace and peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who gathers us into his light, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord Jesus, you are the Lamb who was slain and yet lives. Lord, have mercy.
Christ Jesus, you see the offering of the poor and the secret movements of the heart. Christ, have mercy.
Lord Jesus, you call us to follow you wherever you go. Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Lord, this is the people that longs to see your face.
homily:
Imagine standing on a quiet, high mountain path, the air crisp and thin, the world below falling away into a soft, blue haze. In the Book of Revelation, John describes such a mountain—Mount Zion—but it is not a place of solitude. It is a place of gathering. He sees the Lamb standing there, and around him, a great multitude. They are singing a new hymn, a sound that John struggles to describe because it is unlike anything of this earth. He says it is like the sound of rushing water, like a loud peal of thunder, and yet, simultaneously, like harpists playing their harps. It is a symphony of power and tenderness, of majesty and intimacy. It is the sound of a home that has finally been reached.

I want you to hold onto this image: the sound of the harp. Think of the way a harpist plays—not by striking the strings with force, but by plucking them with precision, with a gentle, deliberate touch. It requires a quiet room to hear the nuance of the notes. It requires a heart that is still enough to listen to the melody. Think of Benjamin Vo. Think of the way he moved through the world—not with the loud, clattering noise of someone trying to be seen, but with the quiet, melodic precision of a boy who understood how things worked. He was a boy of logic, a boy who loved the clean, structured lines of code, the architecture of a Boeing 737, the systems that make the world fly. But there was a music to his soul that was even more profound. It was the music of a gentle heart, a boy who could look at his parents and his brother, Ryan, and simply be present, simply be love. He was like a string on a harp, tuned to the frequency of kindness, vibrating with a sweetness that everyone who knew him could hear, even if they couldn't always put it into words.

Let us tell the truth of the heart before we look for the comfort. Alan, Thao, Ryan, and all of you who hold the memory of Benjamin as a sacred trust: five months have passed. The calendar page turns, but the heart often stays in the room where he last smiled. We know the reality of your quiet house. We know the moments when the silence becomes a weight, when the habits of a lifetime—the quick laugh, the bright smile, the way he would share his dreams of 'con chim airlines'—are suddenly met with an empty space. You are grieving. You are carrying a cross that is heavy, real, and unrelenting. You are allowed to be tired. You are allowed to feel the sudden ache when a memory ambushes you in the middle of an ordinary day. Do not pretend the weight is lighter than it is. Do not rush to be ‘strong’ for the sake of others if your heart is currently breaking. Your honesty before God is the most authentic prayer you can offer. Your tears are not a lack of faith; they are the language of love that has no place left to go.

And let us gently lift one particular stone from your hearts today—a stone that grief often slips into our pockets without us noticing. Sometimes, when a family suffers an unimaginable loss, the mind begins to circle back, whispering quiet, unfair questions. Did we miss a sign? Could we have done something more? Could we have watched closer? Let us lay that burden down right here at the altar. You missed nothing. You loved Benjamin with a completeness that filled his fifteen years with the richness of a lifetime—traveling the globe together, sharing quiet stories, and walking side by side as a family of four. You were the exact parents and the exact brother that Benjamin needed. Let that heavy stone fall; you are absolved, and you are held. You did not fail him in any way. You were the light in his life, just as he was the light in yours. Some things in this life are simply beyond our control, and God does not hold you responsible for the mysteries of the cross. You are held in His mercy, not judged by your sorrow. You are not to blame for the randomness of the world’s living. You are simply loved.

Now, let the Gospel break into that quiet room. Jesus looks up and sees the treasury. He sees the wealthy throwing in large sums, but his eyes are drawn to the widow. She gives two small coins. It is a tiny, almost invisible offering. But Jesus says she gave more than all the rest. Why? Because she gave from her poverty, not her surplus. She gave her whole livelihood. She gave everything. This is the hinge of the mystery. We often think that our offering to God must be something grand, something loud, something that the world can see. But Jesus points to the widow to show us that the only currency that matters in the Kingdom is the heart that is poured out completely. Benjamin understood this. He was a boy who, in his own way, offered his entire self. Think of that moment, unprompted, when he wanted to hand over his entire piggy bank to help his uncle William. He didn't need to break it, he didn't need to empty it; the offering itself was the harp string vibrating in the presence of God. It was the pure, unadulterated desire to be a blessing to someone else. That is the offering that God receives. That is the melody that joins the song before the throne.

Consider the image of the harp again. In the Book of Revelation, the ones who follow the Lamb are the ones who have his name on their foreheads. They are the ones who have been ransomed. They are the ones who sing the new hymn. Benjamin is among them now. He is standing on Mount Zion, and he is singing that song. He is not a memory tucked away in a photo album; he is a living soul in the Banquet of Heaven. He is fully alive, fully restored, and fully embraced by the Father. He is the boy who loved to dream, the boy who giggled at the idea of his own airline, the boy who looked at the world with such profound curiosity. He is all of that, and he is with the God of the living. He is the firstfruits of the promise, waiting for the day when the family of four is whole again. He is watching over you with a love that has been purified and perfected. Think of the dream Alan had, where you and Ben were standing outside room 419, and he said with that earnest, familiar voice, 'Ba ơi, test nào con cũng qua hết... Không sao đâu, con sẽ dõi theo ba mẹ.' That dream was a whisper from heaven. It was the assurance that he has passed every test, that he is whole, and that he is watching over you with a smile. He is the one who has already crossed the threshold into the light, and he is cheering you on.

Ryan, you are a brother who carries a unique, holy weight. You know the memories better than anyone. You know the games you coded, the dreams you shared, the simple, everyday life of being brothers. You are not just a brother who remains; you are a brother who continues the story. When you look at the sky, when you think of the future, remember that you are not doing it alone. You are carrying the legacy of his joy. You are a witness to the world that love is not a finite resource. It is a well that never runs dry. Keep being the boy who reaches out. Keep being the one who values the small, human moments. You are a vital part of this family of four, and your life is a testament to the fact that love is the most durable thing we possess. Your brother's love is not gone; it is woven into the very fabric of who you are becoming. He is cheering for you, and he is walking with you in the quiet places of your heart. You are the one who carries his laughter forward. You are the one who keeps the melody alive.

To everyone tuning in from afar—especially other children who are carrying heavy crosses of suffering, and every family whose home feels too quiet today—hear this: you are seen by God. You are not forgotten. The Lord draws closest to the brokenhearted, and His mercy is broad enough to hold every single one of our tears. You are not a broken family. You are a family of four, and you are being held in the palm of God's hand. The Lamb who was slain is the Lamb who is risen, and he is the one who promises that one day, every tear will be wiped away, and we will hear that new hymn, and we will see clearly that love was the only thing that ever mattered. The God of the living is the God who is with you right now in this very room, in the silence, in the ache, and in the hope that refuses to die.

So, what do you carry out the door today? Not a summary, not a heavy burden, but one small, doable thing: when the grief rises and the house feels too quiet, pause. Close your eyes. Breathe in. Imagine the Lord reaching into the silence, and imagine Benjamin standing beside you, smiling that bright, easy grin, looking out toward an endless horizon, dreaming of his next journey. Let yourself be gathered into the peace of Christ. Walk out knowing that you are loved, that you are not to blame, and that the one who went before you is waiting at the door of eternity. Keep your heart open to that truth. Keep your eyes on the light. And remember that he is watching over you, always, with love that knows no end. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, may his face shine upon you and be gracious to you, and may he give you his peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
petition_call: For all our needs, we pray to the Lord.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Benjamin and all who have gone before us marked with the sign of faith, that they may rest in the eternal light and peace of Christ.
For all who grieve, that the Lord may console them with his presence and grant them the hope of the Resurrection.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
I, John, looked and there was the Lamb standing on Mount Zion,
and with him a hundred and forty-four thousand
who had his name and his Father’s name written on their foreheads.
I heard a sound from heaven
like the sound of rushing water or a loud peal of thunder.
The sound I heard was like that of harpists playing their harps.
They were singing what seemed to be a new hymn before the throne,
before the four living creatures and the elders.
No one could learn this hymn except the hundred and forty-four thousand
who had been ransomed from the earth.
These are the ones who follow the Lamb wherever he goes.
They have been ransomed as the first fruits
of the human race for God and the Lamb.
On their lips no deceit has been found; they are unblemished.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R.        (see 6) Lord, this is the people that longs to see your face.The LORD’s are the earth and its fullness;
the world and those who dwell in it.
For he founded it upon the seas
and established it upon the rivers.R.        Lord, this is the people that longs to see your face.Who can ascend the mountain of the LORD?
or who may stand in his holy place?
He whose hands are sinless, whose heart is clean,
who desires not what is vain.R.        Lord, this is the people that longs to see your face.He shall receive a blessing from the LORD,
a reward from God his savior.
Such is the race that seeks for him,
that seeks the face of the God of Jacob.R.        Lord, this is the people that longs to see your face.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
When Jesus looked up he saw some wealthy people
putting their offerings into the treasury
and he noticed a poor widow putting in two small coins.
He said, “I tell you truly,
this poor widow put in more than all the rest;
for those others have all made offerings from their surplus wealth,
but she, from her poverty, has offered her whole livelihood.”

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: I miss you so much Ben! Ba má nhớ con rất nhiều mỗi ngày.
Nha Trang, ngày 31/10/2026, anh Minh suy nghĩ về Ben rất nhiều. Nhớ và thương em!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - mom and I have been missing you a lot.   Saw you a few times in my dreams last few weeks! Come and say hi daily okay?
Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
